observation.visible_scene: A static, high-angle view of a light wood floor. The upper half is filled with a fan-shaped arrangement of domino piles sorted into rainbow color bands (purple, dark blue, light blue, green, yellow, orange, red, pink), with scattered loose pieces around them. The lower half contains several long serpentine/wavy lines of multicolored standing dominoes, including two braided wavy rows near the middle, one row forming a U-turn on the left, and one long row along the bottom edge. A white braided cord lies on the far left, a transparent ruler sits horizontally above the foreground lines, and short rows of white dominoes are laid out on the right. A baseboard, a valve, and a black clamp are fixed at the top.
visible_changes: During the clip, sections of the foreground serpentine domino lines change from upright zigzag rows into lying-down (toppled) rows, i.e. a toppling wave is progressing along one or more of these lines.

The upright-to-flat transition advances/shifts along the wavy rows over time (e.g. the middle wavy row and the row with the left U-turn show standing segments in early frames becoming flattened or diagonal-fallen segments in later frames).
The large rainbow color piles in the background remain undisturbed and in the same positions throughout the excerpt.
The white cord, transparent ruler, white domino rows on the right, and the background wall/valve/clamp show no change.
The camera framing is fixed; the background reference points (valve, black clamp, baseboard) do not move, so observed changes are object motion, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the toppling and whether the chain reaction continues past the end of the segment.
The full extent of the domino layout outside the frame.
Whether the toppled lines were previously part of a longer continuous chain.
uncertain_details: The exact propagation direction and speed of the toppling wave along the wavy lines is hard to pin down from the sampled frames.
Some small apparent differences between adjacent frames may be compression artifacts rather than real motion.
It is not fully certain which specific line (top braid vs. middle wavy vs. U-turn row) is actively toppling at each moment; the change is gradual and localized.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
